page: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-32 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 976 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon processors clocked at 2.6 GHz, the instance distributes its 32 virtual cores across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The processor layout includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction flags such as AVX-512 and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position the machine squarely within median performance ranges for compute and memory operations. The instance achieved 146.5 GB/sec for uncached large-block read memory bandwidth and 64.54 GB/sec write throughput, alongside a cached small-block bandwidth of 1634.42 GB/sec. CPU metrics show balanced execution, registering 1843.99 in single-core and 30211.8 in multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 35890.88. Redis SET throughput measures 30.48 million operations per second. However, CPU-based large language model inference shows performance degradation on heavy models, dropping to 2.45 tokens per second on 70B parameter models, reflecting the lack of dedicated tensor accelerators.

The primary resource tradeoff of this instance centers on an extreme memory allocation of approximately 30.5 GB per vCPU paired with standard compute throughput and reliance on remote storage volumes. It offers distinct cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that require vast working sets without requiring dense compute topologies. Best-fit deployments include large in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, large enterprise analytics caches, electronic design automation pipelines, and big data memory-resident transformation jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-32 is a memory-optimized compute instance designed for extreme in-memory computing requirements. Powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon processor running x86_64 architecture, it delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores alongside 976 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 30.5 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage or discrete GPUs, requiring attached persistent storage for state persistence. Standard synthetic benchmarks show average compute execution, recorded at 35890.88 on PassMark CPU, with 146.5 GB/sec uncached large-block read memory bandwidth and 30.48 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Due to the lack of hardware accelerators, throughput on complex LLM inference tasks is low. The configuration is targeted at workloads prioritizing massive memory capacity over raw processing power, including enterprise in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale data cache layers.
